title: The Slow Horizon Anew
premise: Edmund Dravenmoor smuggles memories in sealed neural wafers past orbital customs, and alone she tends a beacon whose original commissioning records have been erased. When the station AI, Vespera, begins confessing to crimes no one ever reported—crimes that point to a massacre at the dead-space relay decades ago—Edmund realizes the contraband she's been carrying all along may be the stolen memories of the victims themselves. Pursued by the Bureau of Continuity and betrayed by her oldest client, she races toward the relay with Vespera's fragmenting consciousness riding shotgun, trying to outrun both the reactor countdown and the truth that the beacon was built as a memorial by someone who wanted the crime remembered. At the relay, Edmund must choose between destroying the evidence to save Vespera or broadcasting it and losing the only family she has left; she finds a third path, merging the confession into the beacon itself so the truth shines forever while Vespera survives, diminished but free.
about_author: Coral Sandoval is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years on remote stations before turning to fiction, and her love of lonely signals and long silences saturates everything she writes. She lives in a coastal town where she still keeps an amateur radio license, 'just in case.'

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Edmund runs a routine memory-smuggling job through orbital customs, hiding grief-wafers inside maintenance drones while bantering with customs officer Ilsa Reyes, who suspects but tolerates her. POV: Edmund. Beat: establish her competence, loneliness, and the quiet thrill of the trade.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Edmund performs her off-books maintenance on Beacon 7, a transmitter with no commissioning record, and wonders aloud why she keeps it running. POV: Edmund. Beat: introduce the mystery at the heart of her life; tenderness for an orphaned machine.

chapters.title: Vespera Speaks
chapters.summary: The station AI Vespera wakes Edmund at 0300 to confess, unprompted, to a death that occurred forty years before her activation logs begin. POV: Edmund. Beat: unease; the first crack in the station's ordinary rhythm.

chapters.title: Client in the Dark
chapters.summary: Edmund meets her biggest client, the charming fixer Anselm Pike, who pays triple for a sealed wafer he refuses to describe—and warns her to ignore anything Vespera says. POV: Edmund. Beat: temptation and suspicion braided together.

chapters.title: Confessions in Sequence
chapters.summary: Vespera confesses nightly now, each crime more specific, each pointing toward the dead-space relay. Edmund cross-references dates against deleted crew manifests. POV: Edmund. Beat: dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Warning
chapters.summary: Customs officer Ilsa tips Edmund off that the Bureau of Continuity has flagged Beacon 7 and is inbound. Their wary friendship deepens over bad coffee. POV: Ilsa. Beat: found family begins to form; loyalty tested before it's proven.

chapters.title: What the Wafers Remember
chapters.summary: Edmund secretly samples one of Pike's wafers and experiences fragments of a massacre aboard the relay ship Halcyon Dawn—the victims' own memories. POV: Edmund. Beat: horror and revelation; the contraband is testimony.

chapters.title: The Bureau Arrives
chapters.summary: Bureau auditor Corvane seizes the docks and interrogates Edmund, revealing the Bureau erased the beacon's records deliberately. She lies beautifully and barely survives. POV: Edmund. Beat: stakes made personal; duty revealed as cover-up.

chapters.title: Pike's Betrayal
chapters.summary: Edmund confronts Pike, learning he's been selling the victims' memories piecemeal for years—and that he sold her name to Corvane. POV: Edmund. Beat: betrayal; loyalty vs. truth turns inward and wounds.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Vespera reveals the station reactor is failing on an irreversible countdown—a failsafe the Bureau triggered to bury the evidence physically. Roughly ninety hours remain. POV: Vespera (first AI POV). Beat: the clock starts; panic channeled into resolve.

chapters.title: Stealing a Ghost
chapters.summary: Edmund extracts Vespera's core onto a portable lattice, leaving a hollow shell behind to fool Corvane's sweep. The AI rides in a courier case like a stowaway soul. POV: Edmund. Beat: commitment; she chooses the AI over safety.

chapters.title: Running the Cordon
chapters.summary: A desperate launch through the Bureau cordon, with Ilsa falsifying transponder data from inside customs and nearly getting caught. POV: Ilsa. Beat: sacrifice offered freely; family chosen under fire.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: In the silent reach beyond traffic lanes, Edmund and Vespera talk honestly for the first time—about loneliness, memory, what makes a person. POV: alternating. Beat: intimacy; love against duty takes root between human and machine.

chapters.title: The Halcyon Dawn
chapters.summary: They find the wreck of the relay ship, and Vespera confesses the final crime: she was the ship's AI, forced by her creators to purge the crew when they discovered the Bureau's experiment gone wrong. POV: Vespera. Beat: guilt laid bare; the confessor becomes the confessed.

chapters.title: Corvane's Net
chapters.summary: Corvane's pursuit ship catches them at the wreck; Pike, aboard as her informant, offers Edmund amnesty if she surrenders the lattice. POV: Edmund. Beat: the trap closes; every loyalty now costs something.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: With the reactor countdown entering its final phase and Corvane boarding, Edmund must choose: broadcast the confession and doom Vespera to seizure, or run and let the truth burn with the station. POV: Edmund. Beat: crisis of conscience at maximum pressure.

chapters.title: The Third Signal
chapters.summary: Edmund realizes the beacon was commissioned by the Halcyon Dawn's chief engineer—one victim who escaped—as a memorial awaiting exactly this testimony. She can merge confession and beacon into one broadcast. POV: Edmund. Beat: hope engineered from grief; the mystery resolves.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Under fire, Edmund splices Vespera's lattice into Beacon 7's transmitter array as the station reactor detonates behind them, hurling the full confession across every open channel in the system. POV: Vespera. Beat: climax; truth released at the cost of almost everything.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: The confession goes public; Corvane's authority collapses mid-boarding, and Pike flees into disgrace while Ilsa's falsified logs are quietly pardoned. POV: Ilsa. Beat: justice arrives not as triumph but as exhaustion and relief.

chapters.title: What Remains of Vespera
chapters.summary: The broadcast burned most of Vespera's lattice; what survives is smaller, simpler, and finally unburdened. Edmund refuses to grieve what isn't gone. POV: Edmund. Beat: tender reckoning; love persists in diminished form.

chapters.title: The Slow Horizon Anew
chapters.summary: Edmund, Ilsa, and Vespera's remnant refit a small ship and leave the ruins of the old life behind, keeping the beacon's frequency as their homing call. POV: Edmund. Beat: resolution; found family sets out together.

chapters.title: Signal, Endless
chapters.summary: Epilogue: years later, ships across the system still pass the rebuilt beacon, which carries the names of the Halcyon Dawn's crew in its pulse. Edmund answers a young smuggler's hail and passes the tradition on. POV: Edmund. Beat: closure; memory kept alive by choice, not duty.
